# ISO 26262 Technical Requirements for "Virtual Machine RTOS shall work as expected"

## Context & Approach

Under ISO 26262, a high-level functional requirement like *"Virtual Machine RTOS shall work as expected"* must be **decomposed into verifiable, measurable technical safety requirements**. Below is a structured breakdown.

---

## 1. Temporal Correctness Requirements

| Requirement ID | Technical Requirement |
|---|---|
| TR-VM-01 | The RTOS scheduler shall guarantee task execution within defined **worst-case execution time (WCET)** bounds |
| TR-VM-02 | The RTOS shall provide **deterministic interrupt latency** ≤ [X µs] for safety-critical interrupts |
| TR-VM-03 | Task deadlines shall be met under **maximum CPU load** conditions (e.g., ≥95% load) |
| TR-VM-04 | The VM hypervisor shall not introduce **jitter** exceeding [X µs] on safety partition scheduling |

---

## 2. Spatial & Memory Isolation Requirements

| Requirement ID | Technical Requirement |
|---|---|
| TR-VM-05 | The VM shall enforce **memory partition isolation** — no guest VM shall access memory regions of another guest |
| TR-VM-06 | Stack overflow in one partition **shall not corrupt** another partition's memory space |
| TR-VM-07 | The RTOS shall implement **MPU/MMU enforcement** for each safety partition |
| TR-VM-08 | DMA access shall be restricted via **IOMMU** to authorized memory regions only |

---

## 3. Resource Management Requirements

| Requirement ID | Technical Requirement |
|---|---|
| TR-VM-09 | CPU time allocation per VM partition shall be **bounded and guaranteed** (no starvation of safety partitions) |
| TR-VM-10 | The RTOS shall prevent **priority inversion** in safety-relevant task scheduling |
| TR-VM-11 | Shared hardware resources (timers, peripherals) shall be **arbitrated without race conditions** |
| TR-VM-12 | The hypervisor shall implement **budget enforcement** per partition (e.g., ARINC 653 model) |

---

## 4. Fault Detection & Handling Requirements

| Requirement ID | Technical Requirement |
|---|---|
| TR-VM-13 | The RTOS shall detect **task deadline misses** and report to the safety manager within [X ms] |
| TR-VM-14 | Watchdog mechanisms shall detect **VM/partition lockup** within [X ms] and trigger safe state |
| TR-VM-15 | The RTOS shall detect and handle **exception/fault propagation** across partition boundaries |
| TR-VM-16 | A failed non-safety partition **shall not cause** loss of function in an ASIL-rated partition |
| TR-VM-17 | The RTOS shall log and report **health monitoring events** (task failure, resource exhaustion) |

---

## 5. Hypervisor / Virtualization-Specific Requirements

| Requirement ID | Technical Requirement |
|---|---|
| TR-VM-18 | The hypervisor shall ensure **temporal partitioning** (time-triggered scheduling of VMs) |
| TR-VM-19 | VM **migration or restart** shall not affect safety partition availability |
| TR-VM-20 | The hypervisor shall provide a **certified/qualified** software component per ISO 26262 Part 8 (SEooC) |
| TR-VM-21 | Virtual device emulation shall not introduce **uncontrolled latency** into safety-relevant I/O paths |
| TR-VM-22 | Inter-VM communication channels shall be **bounded in latency and protected** from data corruption |

---

## 6. Freedom from Interference (FFI) Requirements
*(ISO 26262-6, Clause 7.4.14)*

| Requirement ID | Technical Requirement |
|---|---|
| TR-VM-23 | ASIL decomposition across VMs shall demonstrate **freedom from interference** (spatial, temporal, communication) |
| TR-VM-24 | A QM partition fault **shall not propagate** to an ASIL-B/C/D partition |
| TR-VM-25 | Interference channels (shared caches, buses, memory bandwidth) shall be **analyzed and mitigated** |

---

## 7. Startup & Availability Requirements

| Requirement ID | Technical Requirement |
|---|---|
| TR-VM-26 | The RTOS/VM shall complete **safe initialization** within [X ms] of power-on |
| TR-VM-27 | The RTOS shall perform **self-test (BIST/STEST)** of scheduling and memory isolation mechanisms at startup |
| TR-VM-28 | Availability of safety partitions shall meet **FMEDA-derived failure rate targets** (e.g., < 10⁻⁸/h for ASIL D) |

---

## 8. Verification & Testing Requirements
*(Traceability to ISO 26262-6, Table 10)*

```
✔ Unit testing of RTOS scheduler logic (MC/DC coverage per ASIL)
✔ Integration testing of partition isolation under fault injection
✔ Timing analysis: static WCET analysis + measurement-based verification
✔ Resource contention stress testing
✔ Watchdog response time verification
✔ Back-to-back testing of VM communication latency
```

---

## Key ISO 26262 References

| Standard Clause | Relevance |
|---|---|
| **Part 6, Clause 7** | Software design requirements |
| **Part 6, Clause 9** | Software unit design & implementation |
| **Part 9** | ASIL-oriented and safety-oriented analyses |
| **Part 11** | Semiconductor/hardware-dependent software |
| **ISO 26262-6, Table 3** | Notations for software architectural design |
| **ISO/SAE 21434** | If cybersecurity aspects of VM are in scope |

---

## Summary

> The decomposition must ensure that **"works as expected"** is replaced by **measurable, testable criteria** covering timing, isolation, fault handling, and interference — each traceable to a specific ASIL level and verified by appropriate methods per ISO 26262.
